label: is-fix-32-36
topic: Fixing open issues #32 to #36 of fractastical/delphi (patent, optogenetic xenobot variant, Broad fish biologists, funding, Sentry)
summary: None of the five issues is fully resolved: #33 and #35 are partly done, #32 and #34 each wait on one fact from the user, and #36 stays blocked. All five issues were fetched from the GitHub API today; all are open and none has a comment, so there is no reply from the Delphi bot or any other agent. New lookup work was done only for #33 (Europe PMC records for five light-control papers plus the xenobot platform paper, and two searches for light-steered cilia that found nothing). The replies for #32, #34, #35 and #36 consolidate research files already in the repo from 2026-11-12; no funding page, people page or patent page was re-opened today. Three draft reply files are in D:/Users/ashenoy00000/delphi-work/agents4/is-fix-32-36/; nothing was posted, sent or changed in the repo. The suggested funding re-check script was not written (out of time), and tracks/issues/replies/ is a proposed path, not an existing one I confirmed.

findings.claim: #32 Financing, and "license your patent": what patent, and what could be claimed?: NEEDS-AMIT - wrote a draft reply that points to the existing prior-art table, ranks the four claimable subject-matter types (method, file format, geometry, composition; the ranking is my judgement) and states the one missing fact: does a filed patent or provisional application exist, and if so its application number and applicant. No patent office was searched by any person's name.
findings.evidence_quote: is there a filed patent, or is this a plan?
findings.confidence: High that the repo holds no evidence of a filed patent; the patent pages themselves were read by an earlier agent, not re-opened by me.

findings.claim: #33 Bioelectricity nonprofit and the Levin line: an optogenetic, hands-off xenobot variant: PARTLY - light control of contractile tissue is published (a light-following engineered ray, light-driven skeletal-muscle machines, multi-actuator light-controlled biobots) and light-driven bioelectric control exists in frog tadpoles; two quick searches found no paper on light-steered cilia beating or an optogenetic xenobot. Wrote a four-step computation-only first step. Which nonprofit was meant is not answerable publicly; the missing fact is its name.
findings.evidence_quote: swim and phototactically follow a light cue
findings.confidence: Medium: titles and the first ~330 characters of each abstract were read, not full texts. The cilia gap rests on two quick searches (Crossref, Europe PMC) and is not proof of absence.

findings.claim: #34 Broad Institute fish biologists: hypotheses for collaboration: NEEDS-AMIT - wrote a draft reply summarising the already-verified candidates (three zebrafish groups, one with unconfirmed current Broad status), a proposed no-commitment offer and contact order, and the one missing fact: who makes first contact. Nobody was contacted.
findings.evidence_quote: Needs a decision on who makes first contact and with what offer.
findings.confidence: Medium: the candidate list comes from the earlier agent's file; I opened no institutional page today.

findings.claim: #35 Funding opportunities for the paper and the contract: PARTLY - wrote a consolidated table of the nearest deadlines and sizes as recorded on 2026-11-12 (earliest dated item: NSF eMB, March 1 annually), with where to re-verify each. Deadlines were not re-fetched today and the proposed re-check script was not written. Missing fact for eligibility: which legal entity would apply.
findings.evidence_quote: Deadlines go stale; re-verify before acting.
findings.confidence: Low to medium on the dates: they are one day old and second-hand; no funder page was opened in this run.

findings.claim: #36 Sentry: identify the agent-communication platform and connect to it: BLOCKED - the issue has no comments, so no agent or bot has answered the question in it. Wrote a draft reply restating the state and the one missing fact: the URL or product name of the "Sentry" used before and the login that owns it. Nothing was signed up for or logged into.
findings.evidence_quote: this session does not post to or poll any such platform
findings.confidence: High that it is blocked on the user; I did no new web search for the platform.

could_not_find: Any comment on issues #32 to #36: all five comment lists came back empty.
A paper showing optogenetic steering of cilia beating in frog multiciliated cells, or any paper describing an optogenetic xenobot (two quick searches only).
Full texts of the six papers cited for #33: only Europe PMC titles and abstract openings were read.
US patent 12215344 (possible channelrhodopsin-cilia claim): not opened; an earlier agent also failed to read it.
Any filed patent or application belonging to the team: not searched by name.
Today's funding deadlines: no funder page was re-opened; the table is as read on 2026-11-12.
The nonprofit meant by 'Non profit Bioelectricity' in the notes.
Which 'Sentry' was used before, where it lives and who owns the login.
Whether tracks/issues/replies/ exists in the repo: it is a suggested target path only.
One Crossref lookup (Kriegman 2020 pipeline paper) returned a non-JSON response and was not retried.
lay_summary: Five open questions on the project's public to-do list were checked; nobody had replied to any of them yet.
For one of them we looked up real papers: scientists have already steered tiny muscle-powered robots with light, but we found no one steering the frog-cell robots that swim with tiny hairs this way.
For the patent, the fish scientists and the 'Sentry' message system, the computer cannot finish alone; each needs one fact that only the project lead knows.
For the money question we gathered the grant dates found yesterday into one table, but they still need to be checked again before anyone relies on them.
Draft answers were saved as files for the lead to post; nothing was sent to anyone.

glossary.optogenetic: Making cells respond to light by giving them a light-sensitive protein.
glossary.xenobot: A tiny living machine built from frog cells.
glossary.cilia: Tiny moving hairs on a cell's surface that push fluid or move the cell.
glossary.contractile tissue: Tissue that can shorten and pull, such as muscle.
glossary.bioelectricity: Electrical signals that cells use to communicate and control growth.
glossary.Archaerhodopsin: A light-driven protein that pumps charged hydrogen out of a cell.
glossary.channelrhodopsin: A light-opened gate protein that lets charged particles into a cell.
glossary.KillerRed: A protein that kills the cell holding it when lit with green light.
glossary.prior art: Anything already public that could stop a new patent being granted.
glossary.provisional application: An early, cheaper patent filing that holds a date for one year.
glossary.freedom-to-operate: A lawyer's opinion on whether you can sell something without infringing others' patents.
glossary.claim 1: The first and usually broadest statement of what a patent protects.
glossary.composition: A patent claim on what a material is made of.
glossary.nanopublication: A very small, machine-readable published statement with its source attached.
glossary.Lean: A computer program that checks mathematical proofs.
glossary.low-Reynolds swimming: How very small things move in fluid, where stickiness matters more than momentum.
glossary.resistive-force theory: A simple way to calculate the thrust of thin moving hairs in fluid.
glossary.MCP: A standard way for an AI assistant to connect to outside tools.
glossary.OAuth: A login method that grants access without sharing a password.
glossary.DOI: A permanent identifier for a published paper.
glossary.Europe PMC: A free online index of life-science papers.
glossary.Crossref: A registry that links DOIs to paper details.
glossary.associate member: A scientist based at another institution who is affiliated with the Broad Institute.
glossary.letter of intent: A short notice sent to a funder before a full application.
glossary.API credits: Prepaid allowance for using an AI service through code.
glossary.legal entity: The organisation that formally applies for and receives a grant.

recommendations: Ask the user three single facts: (#32) is there a filed patent or provisional, with number and applicant; (#34) who makes first contact; (#36) the URL or product name of the Sentry used before and the login that owns it.
For #33, ask the user for the name of the nonprofit meant in the notes, and pass the computation-only plan to the organism thread, which owns organism-design/.
For #35, re-open each funder page before quoting any deadline, and ask which legal entity would apply.
Post the three draft files as issue comments after the lead reviews them; add a 'needs-user' label to #32, #34 and #36.
